charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Revenue by Channel: Direct to Consumer vs Professional Solutions
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs FCF After Leases
charts.annotation: FCF after leases is the group's own cash-flow-statement measure (OCF less CapEx less lease principal repayments). Owner FCF, shown in the DCF section below, additionally removes SBC and interest income.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. FCF after leases is the group's own cash-flow-statement measure, additionally deducting lease principal repayments (EssilorLuxottica runs ~12,000 owned-and-leased retail stores, so lease principal is a real recurring cash outflow, not a financing curiosity). Owner FCF (shown in the DCF section below) goes further still, also removing stock-based compensation and interest income -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the gap between net income, reported FCF and FCF after leases is almost entirely the retail lease book; watch it widen as DTC (owned stores) grows faster than Professional Solutions (wholesale, asset-light).

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • FCF after leases falling further behind reported FCF as store count grows
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

channelMix.title: Revenue by channel
channelMix.content:
EssilorLuxottica reports revenue by two channels: Direct to Consumer (owned retail and e-commerce -- LensCrafters, Sunglass Hut, Ray-Ban and Oakley stores, GrandVision) and Professional Solutions (wholesale lenses, frames and equipment sold to independent opticians and other retailers).

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the two channels carry different margin and capital profiles -- DTC captures the full retail margin but consumes the lease and store CapEx shown in the cash-flow charts above, while Professional Solutions is asset-light wholesale. DTC has been the faster grower since the 2023 GrandVision integration, so the mix shift is itself a margin and FCF-after-leases driver.

What to watch:

  • DTC share of group revenue rising (more owned stores, more lease liability)
  • Professional Solutions growth as a read on independent-optician demand, decoupled from EssilorLuxottica's own retail footprint

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For EssilorLuxottica SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
